title: service-contract-change-signal-and-safe-fallback-playbook
author: Amina Duarte
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a cross-cutting standard for signaling intentional API contract changes and executing safe fallback behavior across the Redwood inference stack. It ties together API surface design, runtime coding patterns, infra controls, model-serving expectations, observability gates, and performance verification steps. The objective is to allow evolution of request/response contracts while guaranteeing predictable degradation behavior, traceability, and rapid rollback when quality or SLO regressions are detected.

Why this exists

- Contract changes are inevitable: model capabilities, streaming semantics, and cost-tiered payloads will evolve.
- Poorly signaled changes cause silent client failures, high-error rates, and costly rollbacks.
- Cross-layer coordination is required: routing, cache affinity, runtime kernels, and telemetry must cooperate during change windows.

Scope

Applies to: public and internal REST/gRPC/streaming endpoints that carry model invocation payloads, especially generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking APIs. Not intended for front-end-only UI changes.

Owners and Contacts

- Primary owner: API Platform (engineering) — contact: amina.duarte@redwood.ai
- Runtime fallback steward: Serving Runtime team — contact: marco.li@redwood.ai
- Observability owner: Eng Platform — contact: sofia.patel@redwood.ai

Key Principles

1) Explicit capability negotiation: clients must express a minimal capability header for optional features. Backends may return a compatible response and a summary of accepted capabilities.
2) Non-breaking defaults: server-side additions must preserve existing fields unless an explicit opt-in signal is present.
3) Fail-safe fallbacks: when a new field or variant is not understood by downstream components, the request must either (a) fall back to a conservative variant, or (b) return a clear 4xx/422 with guidance.
4) Observable contract transitions: every change window must emit structured telemetry: change_id, gating_metric, rollforward/rollback decisions.

Contract Signaling Specification

Headers and Metadata

- X-Redwood-Contract: semantic token representing contract version (e.g., contract.v2.render-hints)
- X-Redwood-Contract-Intent: comma-separated capabilities the client is requesting (e.g., structured-output,stream-multiplex)
- X-Redwood-Client-Approx: optional perf hint (fast|balanced|high-fidelity) used by routing and kernel selectors

Request Body Schema Rules

1. Additive-only for opt-in fields: new optional fields must be namespaced under 'opt' or 'features'.
2. Required fields may only be added after a staged rollout and with explicit deprecation windows.

Sample header example

curl -X POST \ \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Contract: contract.v2.render-hints' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Contract-Intent: structured-output,function-calls' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Fallback Patterns (ranked by recommendation)

1) Variant Downgrade (preferred): map the request to a previous model variant or quantization profile that maintains semantics.
2) Partial Response + Hints: return a partial structured response with a top-level 'incomplete: true' flag and diagnostic suggestion.
3) Reject-with-guidance: return 422 with a structured error pointing to required contract capabilities and a suggested client fix.

Implementation Checklist (developer-facing)

- API: validate X-Redwood-Contract and X-Redwood-Contract-Intent; log mismatches at info level with change_id.
- Runtime: expose a fast-path for variant downgrade that preserves tokenization and KV cache compatibility.
- Cache: ensure prefix cache keys include contract.version to avoid poisoning.
- Router: make traffic-splitting rules aware of contract token and use weighted fallbacks.
- SDKs: expose helper to query supported capabilities and to opt-in safely.

Observability and Telemetry Gates

Mandatory telemetry emitted for a contract transition window:

- contract.change_id (tag)
- contract.request_count (counter)
- contract.error_rate (p50/p95/p99) per route and per variant
- contract.latency_ms.p95
- contract.fidelity_regressions (derived from eval harness)
- contract.rollback_reason (event)

Alerting thresholds (default)

- Error rate > 2% absolute increase over baseline in first 30 minutes -> P1 alert to oncall.
- 95th latency increase > 50% vs baseline -> P1.
- Fidelity regression (eval set delta) > configured threshold -> block rollout.

Testing and Performance Verification

Before any staged rollout:

1) Unit + contract tests: validate new optional fields deserialize in both new and old code paths.
2) Integration: run canary traffic at 0.5% for 30 minutes with synthetic load.
3) Perf: run 5-minute stress with representative sequence length histogram; capture kernel selection variance.
4) Eval: run a small eval set (100 prompts) comparing outputs against quality gates; track semantic drift via automatic scoring.

Rollout Procedure (numbered)

1. Open a Change Window: register change_id and high-level plan in the rollout registry.
2. Run preflight: run CI checks, integration smoke, and perf profile.
3. Canary 0.5% for 30m: monitor contract metrics and fidelity evals.
4. Gradual expand: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30–60 minute observation at each step.
5. Automatic halt: gate expansion on telemetry; halt if any P1 threshold triggers.
6. Rollback: if halted, execute variant-downgrade path and open incident ticket; capture diagnostics and run postmortem.

Coding and Infra Standards (practical rules)

- Backwards compatibility suites must be part of the pre-merge CI for any API surface change.
- Use feature flags for server-side opt-ins; flags must include owner, expiry date, and test coverage.
- Prefix cache key and KV layout with contract.version and variant.id.
- Runtime sidecar must support a /compat endpoint that returns current supported contract tokens and capability matrix.

Model-serving expectations

- Model artifacts must include a capability manifest (manifest.json) listing supported contract tokens, max_sequence, quantization profile, and deterministic_hash.
- When serving multiple variants, maintain a compatibility ledger that maps variant->compatible-seed-versions for KV cache reuse.

Decision Record (ADR) — summary of tradeoffs

Decision ID: ADR-2027-04-contract-signal
Date: 2026-11-14
Decision: Require explicit contract headers and conservative fallback by default.
Reasoning: Implicit changes were causing silent client breakages and made incident triage slow. Explicit headers improve observability and allow deterministic routing to compatible variants.
Consequences: Slightly larger request surface (extra headers), additional runtime checks, more complex cache keying. Long-term benefit: faster rollouts, fewer P1 incidents.

Appendix: Quick reference table

| Field | Purpose | Required during rollout? | Default behavior |
|-------|---------|--------------------------|------------------|
| X-Redwood-Contract | Contract token | Yes | When missing, server treats as contract.v1 (legacy) |
| X-Redwood-Contract-Intent | Opt-in capabilities | No | Missing intent => conservative processing |
| contract.change_id (telemetry) | Traceable rollout id | Yes | Populated by router during change window |

Sample compatibility policy (YAML)

---
fallback_policies:
  - name: variant-downgrade
    match_order: [structured-output,stream-multiplex,function-calls]
    fallback_to: previous_stable_variant

Questions and escalation

- For rollout help, open an issue in #api-rollouts Slack channel and tag @api-platform.
- If a P1 triggers during a change window, follow the Incident Playbook and notify the oncall SRE.
